correctness.rationale: Root containment agrees with complete-square containment: copy an embedding twice in one direction; in the other, if the first embedded X ends in the first Y, use it, otherwise the entire second X lies in the second Y. The first X need not literally cross the junction, but the suffix argument still applies. A mixed deficient root needs length at least two and a maximum root needs length at least three. At host length six, the only possible length-three square fills the host, so every shorter root is contained in its root. At length seven, if the deficient root is 10, a feasible root of length three must avoid 10, hence lies in {000,001,011,111}; the unary options leave too few letters of the other kind for 1010. A bounded independent insertion check gives the following complete list among insertions that contain 1010: from 001001, hosts 0010010, 0010101, 0101001, 1001001, where the first and last are rejected by extensions 010 and 100; from 011011, hosts 0101011, 0110101, 0110110, 1011011, where the last two are rejected by extensions 110 and 101. Complementing gives the other four qualifying words; their stated reversal/complementation orbits follow. A separate bounded census of all 255 binary hosts through length seven agreed. In Wₘ the two ones force each mixed root to have exactly one 1; if the root is 0ᵃ10ᵇ then its square must fit a+b zeros in the single central zero position. Thus 10 embeds as a square and cannot extend; all mixed roots have length at most two. The 2m+1 zeros and two ones then give maximum root length m for m≥3.
residual_risks: The census is exhaustive only through length seven. The separate central-gap proof gives the infinite family; the reviewed claim does not identify all maximal roots in arbitrary larger inputs.

value.rationale: Recent maximal-square algorithms make it natural to ask how small a binary input can already contain a genuinely mixed maximal solution shorter than the maximum and whether the distinction can be arbitrarily large. A smallest-host classification with all equality cases and an all-m fixed-two-marker construction answer these questions; the mixed requirement rules out trivial unary deficiencies. The quantitative statements add to the known qualitative overlap without claiming to predict any algorithm's output.
residual_risks: No approximation claim is made about an algorithm for selecting a maximal square, and no optimal ratio as a function of arbitrary host length is asserted.
